definition: Yummly was an American website and mobile app that provided users recipes via recommendations and a search engine.
details: Yummly used a knowledge graph to offer a semantic web search engine for food, cooking and recipes.

explainer.lead: Yummly was an American website and mobile app that recommended recipes and offered a recipe search engine. It used a knowledge graph to power semantic search over food and cooking.

tiers.eli5: It was a recipe site that understood what you meant, so searching for a dish found sensible matches rather than just matching words.
tiers.practitioner: It is a product example rather than a method, showing how a knowledge graph supports semantic search in a consumer app. A pitfall in such designs is keeping the graph's food and recipe data current.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition applies; it is a recommendation and semantic search product built on a food knowledge graph, limited by the coverage and upkeep of that graph.

explainer.example: A user searching for a dish gets recipes ranked by meaning rather than exact keyword overlap, thanks to the knowledge graph.
